title: The Way Down
description:
Daeun brought it up carefully.
"Minjun... this weekend, could you come down to the countryside with me? My mom has a hospital appointment."

Two train tickets. They sat side by side at the window. Seoul slid backward; rice paddies filled the glass.

After staring out the window a long while, Daeun spoke.
"Minjun, honestly — I'm scared."
"I came up to Seoul to be able to take care of her someday... and lately I'm not sure that's even a thing that can happen."

For the first time, the reason she'd held on for five years came out of her mouth with weight.

choices.text: "Whatever happens, I'll be right beside you." (Take her hand)
choices.result_text:
Daeun looked down at the hand holding hers. And smiled, a little.
"...You say things like that so easily, Minjun."
"I'm not saying it easily." When {name} said that, Daeun leaned her head against the window instead of answering.
The train kept going down, toward her hometown.

choices.text: Say nothing, and look out the window with her.
choices.result_text:
{name} said nothing. Instead, he looked where she was looking.

Instead of answering 'scared' with 'it'll be fine,' he just sat beside that fear.
After a long while Daeun said, quietly, "...It's a little easier, you looking at it with me."
The train kept going down, toward her hometown.

title: Her Mother's Table
description:
After the appointment, they had dinner at Daeun's country home.

Her mother wasn't one for words. Instead she kept heaping more rice into {name}'s bowl. "Eat more. You can't get food like this up in Seoul."

Then, out of nowhere, her mother glanced at {name}'s hands.
"...Hands that have worked hard."

In the middle of the table sat a gyeran-mari, the rolled omelet — yellow, thick, the ends neatly folded.
{name} knew that shape. It was the very same rolled omelet Daeun used to bring to his goshiwon in a side-dish container.
Without a word, he understood where it had come from.

choices.text: "Thank you for the meal, Mother." Finish the bowl with care.
choices.result_text:
{name} finished the bowl without leaving a single grain. Her mother saw it, and smiled for the first time, a little.

The night bus back. Daeun slept leaning against the window.
In one pane, the receding lights of the countryside and the approaching lights of Seoul were held together.

There had been nights spent counting three billion won. Tonight, for the first time, was a night he didn't have to count.

choices.text: "...So the gyeran-mari you used to make — it was your mother's."
choices.result_text:
Daeun stopped her chopsticks. Her face went a little red.
"...I copied hers. I'm still not as good as her."
At those words, her mother looked at her daughter for a long moment.

The night bus back. Daeun slept leaning against the window.
In one pane, the receding lights of the countryside and the approaching lights of Seoul were held together.

There had been nights spent counting three billion won. Tonight, for the first time, was a night he didn't have to count.

description_if_known.father_passed:
After the appointment, they had dinner at Daeun's country home.

Her mother wasn't one for words. Instead she kept heaping more rice into {name}'s bowl.
Then she asked, "And your parents, Minjun — what do they do?"

{name} lost his answer for a moment. His father was gone now. Not knowing what to say, he just looked at his bowl.
Her mother must have read the silence; she didn't ask again, only glanced at {name}'s hands.
"...Hands that have worked hard."

In the middle of the table sat a gyeran-mari, the rolled omelet — the very same one Daeun used to bring to his goshiwon.
Without a word, he understood where it had come from.

title: Three Days of Silence
description:
Three days, and no word from Jiyeon.

She was never one to reach out first. Still, three days was long.

Eleven at night. A knock at the door — Jiyeon, standing outside it.
No makeup, eyes that hadn't slept in days.

"...Oppa." She searched for the words a moment.
"Turns out tonight, this was the only place I had to go."

The woman who always looked down from the height of her own world stood, for the first time, lowered — outside {name}'s narrow door.

choices.text: Ask nothing, and open the door.
choices.result_text:
{name} asked nothing and stepped aside.
Jiyeon took off her shoes and came in. She looked once around the narrow room, then just sat on the floor.

"...You're not even going to ask."
"Do I have to?" When {name} said that, Jiyeon let the tension out of her shoulders for the first time.

choices.text: "What happened?" Ask without hiding the worry.
choices.result_text:
"What happened?" When {name} asked, Jiyeon let out a small laugh.
"...Of course that's the first thing you'd ask."
She didn't answer. Instead she took off her shoes, came in, and sat on the narrow room's floor.
"I'll stay a bit. ...That okay?"
{name} nodded.

description_if_known.arc_y3_jiyeon_departure_seen:
Three days, and no word from Jiyeon. With her down in Busan, contact was always sparse to begin with.

Still, three days was long.

Eleven at night. A knock at the door — Jiyeon, standing outside it.
The face of someone who'd taken the last late-night KTX up from Busan. No makeup, eyes that hadn't slept in days.

"...Oppa." She searched for the words a moment.
"Turns out tonight, this was the only place I had to go."

She'd left the wide house in Busan, caught the last train up, and the place she ended up standing was outside {name}'s narrow door.
The woman who always looked down from the height of her own world stood, for the first time, lowered.

title: The Narrow Room
description:
She sat in the narrow room, designer coat tossed off to one side, knees drawn up.

{name} poured water into two cup ramyeon. There was nothing else to offer.

Jiyeon looked slowly around the room. A few books, a folded blanket, one window. By the standards of her world, a room with nothing in it.

"This room is like you, oppa," she said.
"It's narrow... but all of it is real. My house is wide, and there's barely anything real in it."

Steam rose off the cup ramyeon and fogged the window pale.

choices.result_text:
Instead of words, {name} held her. Jiyeon was stiff at first, then pressed her forehead into his shoulder.

"...The ramyeon's going soft," she said, but for a long while neither of them moved.
That night, the narrow room was exactly two people wide.

choices.text: Say nothing, and finish cooking the ramyeon, and set it down.
choices.result_text:
Instead of answering, {name} set the ramyeon in front of her. "Eat it before it goes soft."
Jiyeon split the wooden chopsticks. One bite, and she snorted a laugh.
"...It's good. Why is this good."
A night sharing two cup ramyeon in a narrow room — for her, it was the first.

description_if_known.told_jiyeon_about_records:
She sat in the narrow room, designer coat tossed off to one side, knees drawn up.

{name} poured water into two cup ramyeon. There was nothing else to offer.

Jiyeon looked slowly around the room. She knows now — whose son the owner of this room is, that the name was on the list her own father had ruined.

"...It's funny." Jiyeon said, looking down at the cup ramyeon.
"I'm eating ramyeon in the room of a man my dad ruined."

A cruelly honest thing to say. She didn't look away from it.
"But this room is like you, oppa. Narrow, and all of it real. My house is wide, and barely anything in it is."

title: The First Night
description:
The wedding over, the night with just the two of them. Their first home — new, boxes still half-unpacked.

At the door Daeun couldn't quite step inside. On the threshold, she kept turning the new ring on her finger with a fingertip. Out of the white dress now, and still, tonight, somehow unfamiliar.

"I..." Her voice was small. She caught her breath once, and still didn't hide it.
"I've never done this before, so — don't laugh."

The tips of her ears flushed red, and still she didn't look away. That was so like Daeun — instead of hiding the shyness, saying, plainly, that she was shy. The air in the room felt a little warmer.
In the face of that honesty, {name} chose how to meet the tension.

choices.text: Take her hand. "We can go slow. I'm... nervous too."
choices.result_text:
"I'm... nervous too." His voice wasn't quite steady either.
Daeun's eyes went wide, then she couldn't help it — she burst out laughing.
"...What. You're the one shaking more, Minjun."
The laughter loosened the taut air like a pulled thread. Inside his hand, her fingers slowly let go of their grip. Their foreheads came close, and Daeun closed her eyes — and the room's light went quietly out.

The next morning. {name} woke to a familiar smell.
Gyeran-mari frying in the kitchen. Daeun, up first, was making breakfast — with those same hands that had trembled the night before.
He watched her back for a long while. The first morning of marriage was beginning with that smell.

choices.text: Make the nervous woman laugh. "Then I'll call it my first time too."
choices.result_text:
"Then tonight, I'll call it my first time too."
Daeun snorted and swatted his arm lightly. "...Where do you even learn to say things like that."
But that one line loosened shoulders that had been stiff as stone. She stepped closer, laughter still on her face, and as the last of the distance between them disappeared — the room's light went quietly out.

Gyeran-mari frying in the kitchen. Daeun, up first, was making breakfast.

description_if_known.daeun_hometown_visited:

{name} took Daeun's hand — the one trembling, just slightly.

title: The First Night
description:
The wedding over, the night with just the two of them. Their new first home.

Jiyeon, always the one quick with words, had none this night. She stood at the window and only looked down at the city. The wine in her hand hadn't dropped a single sip.
The silence of a proud person was a different thing from her pride. {name} knew her well enough, now, to tell the difference.

"...Why are you standing there like that." When {name} came closer, her shoulders drew in, just slightly. In the window's reflection, her face was redder than usual.
Without words, {name} chose how to meet that silence.

choices.text: Respect the silence, and offer his hand first.
choices.result_text:
{name} asked nothing. He simply held out his hand.
Jiyeon looked down at it. One beat, two. The usual her would have already fired off some remark by now. But this night she took the hand without a word. The fingers that closed on his trembled, faintly — and it wasn't the wine.
When {name} drew the hand gently toward him, she came without resisting. The city lights outside blurred over the two of them — and the room's light went quietly out.

The next morning. Waking beside her, {name} saw a face he'd never seen.
Makeup all wiped away, eyes a little puffy, bare — not a piece of the armor she always kept perfectly in place. Jiyeon felt the look and pulled the blanket up to her nose.
"...What are you staring at. Mornings are just like this."
The voice was curt, but above the blanket the tips of her ears were red. {name} had to work not to smile.

choices.text: Tease the nerves she couldn't hide. "The great Han Jiyeon, out of words."
choices.result_text:
"The great Han Jiyeon, out of words." When {name} said it, Jiyeon whipped around.
"...Shut up." A snap — but at the end of it, the stiffness in her face eased a little. As if being caught nervous were, actually, a relief.
She set the wine down and took a step toward {name}. "...Laugh and you're dead." The voice saying it shook, just slightly.
The room's light went quietly out.
